front_door.content:
<!-- docs-structure: start here -->
## Start here

Two files, in this order. Everything else is one hop from the last one.

1. **This file** - what mini-app is and how the repository is laid out.
2. **[docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md)** - the index of every doc: what each one owns and its state. Pick the one file you need there; do not read the folder.

From the index, the usual first stops: [how to run it](docs/setup.md), [the architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) (skeleton), [the plan](docs/TASKLIST.md) (skeleton). The index says which file is which; this README keeps no list of its own, so the two cannot drift.

The docs have a shape and a checker: one central index, an owner line on every doc, no line-number citations. `docs_structure.py --repo .` from the docs-structure skill checks it; `docs/structure.json` is its manifest.
<!-- /docs-structure: start here -->
front_door.where: after the intro paragraph under the H1, before the first H2; replace what sits between the markers on refill
front_door.why: so the front door hands off to the index in the same three-step shape on every repo (R11)

index_rows: | [PRODUCT](PRODUCT.md) | what the product is, who it is for, where it is going, and what it has said no to. | skeleton |
| [ARCHITECTURE](ARCHITECTURE.md) | the services, their boundaries, the data flow between them, and the key decisions with their dates. | skeleton |
| [TASKLIST](TASKLIST.md) | the index of the plan — one file per phase under `tasklist/`, and the count of todo / doing / done in each. | skeleton |
| [DEPLOYMENT](DEPLOYMENT.md) | how the system is deployed — every service, its environment, the steps, and how to roll back. | skeleton |
| [TESTING](TESTING.md) | how this repository is tested — the runners, where tests live, how to run them, and what CI checks. | skeleton |
| [RUNBOOK](RUNBOOK.md) | how this system is run in production — health checks, scheduled jobs, alerts, and what to do when each one fires. | skeleton |

print_only.AGENTS.md:
## Docs routing - where a change gets written down

One doc owns each fact; the others link. Every doc's header says what it owns. When you change
one of these, update the owner in the same change.

| you changed... | update |
|---|---|
| what the product is for, who it serves, or something it decided not to do | [docs/PRODUCT.md](docs/PRODUCT.md) |
| a service boundary, a link between services, or a decision worth a date | [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) |
| a setup step, a prerequisite version, or a daily command | [docs/setup.md](docs/setup.md) |
| a task starting, finishing or being dropped | [docs/TASKLIST.md](docs/TASKLIST.md) |
| a service, an environment variable, a build or start command, a deploy step | [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) |
| a test runner, where tests live, how to run them, or what gates a merge | [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md) |
| a health check, a scheduled job, an alert, or what to do when one fires | [docs/RUNBOOK.md](docs/RUNBOOK.md) |

Rules that keep this true:

- Cite symbols and log tags, never line numbers - `file.ts:123` rots within one change.
- Strike superseded figures (`~~old~~ -> new`), do not delete them.
- Every doc has a row in `docs/INDEX.md` and a `> **This document owns:**` line under its H1.
- `python <skill-dir>/scripts/docs_structure.py --repo . --fail-on-findings` is the check.
